content.text:
Done. Both routes render (200s — the nonzero exit code is just the server cleanup), and the build passes type-checking with the experiment enabled. Here's what I added:

**Setup**
- `next.config.ts` — enabled `experimental.viewTransition`, which activates React's `<ViewTransition>` component for App Router navigations. This Next canary's vendored React exports it as plain `ViewTransition` (no `unstable_` prefix), and it works in Server Components, so no `'use client'` boundaries were needed.
- `react-canary.d.ts` — a triple-slash reference to `react/canary` so TypeScript knows about the `ViewTransition` export.

**Shared element morph** — in `app/ProductGrid.tsx` each thumbnail and in `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` the hero image are wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={'product-image-' + slug} share="product-morph">`. Because the names match across the two pages, React pairs them during navigation and the browser morphs position/size between the thumbnail and the large image. The `product-morph` class gets a 350ms eased timing in CSS.

**Directional slides** — the home page is wrapped in `<ViewTransition enter="page-from-left" exit="page-to-left">` and the detail page in the mirror-image `enter="page-from-right" exit="page-to-right"`. So going grid → detail, the grid slides out left while the detail slides in from the right (forward motion); going back, everything reverses — no direction-tracking state needed. The morphing image is captured in its own group, so it glides independently while the pages slide. I also wrapped the detail page content in `<main>` (it was a bare `<div>` before) so both pages share the same width/padding and the slide lines up.

**Suspense reveals** — both Suspense boundaries (the grid on home, the product info on detail) are wrapped in `<ViewTransition update="suspense-reveal">`, so the skeleton-to-content swap runs as a 250ms cross-fade instead of an instant pop. The detail page's boundary (with its 100ms artificial delay) is the one you'll actually see animate.

**Reduced motion** — a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block in `globals.css` sets `animation: none` on all `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements (view transitions don't respect the preference automatically), making every navigation an instant swap, and also stops the skeleton pulse animation.

To see it live: `npm run dev`, click any product card and use "← Back to products" — the colored image morphs between layouts while the page slides. Toggle "reduced motion" in your OS or DevTools rendering settings to confirm everything becomes instant.
